full_text_en:
Nobel Co., Ltd. v. ADI Limited, Lung Yuen International (Hong Kong) Limited, and CEIEC (Hong Kong) Limited — Dispute over Purchase and Sale Contract

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Wuxi Nobel Computer Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 7 Xizhi Street, Wuxi, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Ruiwu, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agents ad litem: Cai Xiaoming, Lin Zhiming, lawyers of Wuxi Liangxi Law Firm, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: ADI Limited (ADVANCED DIGITAL INTERNATIONAL LIMITED). Domicile: Minle Street, Hung Hom, Kowloon, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Jian Yuxiang, Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Lung Yuen International (Hong Kong) Limited (LUNGYUEN INTERNATIONAL (HONG KONG) LIMITED). Domicile: Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Zheng Dong, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Xu Zhenying, lawyer of Nanjing Zijin Law Firm.

Defendant: CEIEC (Hong Kong) Limited (CEIEC (HONG KONG) LIMITED). Domicile: Wan Chai Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Xue Yongshou, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Fan Wenjiang, Deputy Manager of CEIEC (Hong Kong) Limited.

Plaintiff Jiangsu Wuxi Nobel Computer Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nobel Company) filed a lawsuit with the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province due to a dispute over a purchase and sale contract with defendants ADI Limited (hereinafter referred to as ADI Company), Lung Yuen International (Hong Kong) Limited (hereinafter referred to as Lung Yuen Company), and CEIEC (Hong Kong) Limited (hereinafter referred to as CEIEC Company).

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff entered into a four-party agreement with the defendants ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, and CEIEC Company, whereby ADI Company authorized Lung Yuen Company, and Lung Yuen Company further authorized the plaintiff as the sole exclusive distributor of PAGE-4W printers manufactured by OKI Company in the domestic market. After the agreement was signed, the plaintiff invested heavily in advertising to launch the market and received 650 printers shipped by Lung Yuen Company, for which it paid RMB 338,692. However, the plaintiff later discovered that ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company had no right at all to grant the plaintiff the right to be the sole exclusive distributor of this product in the domestic market; the authorization was purely a fraud by ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company against the plaintiff. During this period, CEIEC Company colluded with Lung Yuen Company to change the purchase and sale relationship, thereby profiting from a price difference of HKD 37,500. The plaintiff requests that the four-party agreement be declared invalid, that the plaintiff be allowed to return 521 unsold printers to Lung Yuen Company, that CEIEC Company be ordered to refund the plaintiff RMB 338,692 and the price difference of HKD 37,500, and that ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company compensate the plaintiff for advertising expenses, transportation and postage costs, travel expenses, and loss of anticipated profits totaling RMB 588,085.19. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by the three defendants.

Defendants ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company did not submit written defenses.

Defendant CEIEC Company argued: In the four-party agreement, this defendant was only a guarantor of the plaintiff's payment and never colluded with defendant Lung Yuen Company. Moreover, after learning that the plaintiff had not obtained the sole exclusive distributorship, it repeatedly assisted the plaintiff in requesting defendant ADI Company to issue a letter of authorization. This defendant earnestly performed the four-party agreement and timely opened letters of credit to pay the amount for 700 printers to Lung Yuen Company, but later only recovered the payment for 125 printers. The price difference that the plaintiff claims was obtained by changing the purchase and sale relationship is actually the handling fee that this defendant should collect for fulfilling its guarantee payment obligation. If the court declares the four-party agreement invalid, then Lung Yuen Company shall refund this defendant the payment of HKD 1,408,750; if it is declared valid, then the plaintiff shall pay the amount to this defendant. The party returning the payment shall also pay bank interest of HKD 300,000 and compensate this defendant for all losses suffered.

Facts Found by the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court:

On August 6, 1996, the plaintiff Nobel Company and the defendants ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, and CEIEC Company signed an "Agreement on the Sale of OKI PAGE-4W Printers in the Chinese Market," stipulating that: ADI Company, on behalf of OKI Electric Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as OKI Company), authorized Lung Yuen Company as the China regional agent for OKI PAGE-4W printers, and Lung Yuen Company further authorized Nobel Company as the sole exclusive distributor of the printers in the domestic market; ADI Company would initially provide 500 printers to Nobel Company through Lung Yuen Company by the end of August, with Lung Yuen Company handling import and customs declaration procedures, delivery location being Guangzhou City, delivery price being RMB 3,260 per unit (including VAT); CEIEC Company would issue a 45-day letter of credit guarantee to Lung Yuen Company before August 8; Nobel Company would pay the full amount in RMB to Lung Yuen Company within 40 days after delivery by Lung Yuen Company; Lung Yuen Company would, within three days after receiving payment, be responsible for repaying CEIEC Company's guarantee amount in US dollars; within three months after the contract took effect, Nobel Company would order 500 printers from ADI Company each month, and after three months, the four parties would separately negotiate new marketing plans and order quantities, etc.

After signing the four-party agreement, the plaintiff Nobel Company carried out advertising and promotional activities. In September 1996, it held the '96 OKI Laser Printer New Product Launch and Demonstration in Beijing, and successively placed advertisements in the *People's Daily* and *China Computer News*, bearing the words "Sole Exclusive Distributor in China," and paid a total of RMB 139,350 in advertising expenses. Because customers questioned Nobel Company's status as the sole exclusive distributor, Nobel Company sent letters to defendants ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, and third parties OKI Hong Kong Company, OKI Company's Beijing Office, and OKI Company, inquiring whether it was the sole exclusive distributor of PAGE-4W printers in the Chinese domestic market, and requesting ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, or OKI Company to issue corresponding authorization letters or supporting documents. During this period, defendant CEIEC Company also assisted Nobel Company in requesting proof of sole exclusive distributor status, but ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company were never able to provide such proof. It was not until August 1, 1997, that ADI Company replied in writing to Nobel Company, stating: "It is impossible to authorize your company as the sole agent, the main reason being that your company's sales performance did not meet the data in the agreement." OKI Hong Kong Company replied to Nobel Company on August 26, 1997, stating: "The authorization matter has nothing to do with the headquarters of OKI Japan, OKI Hong Kong Company, or OKI Company's Beijing Office. Please negotiate directly with ADI Company and CEIEC Company to resolve this issue." During litigation, Lung Yuen Company provided the court with proof that ADI Company had been authorized by OKI Hong Kong Company as one of the distributors of PAGE-4W printers in China for the period from June 1, 1996, to May 31, 1997, but was never able to provide proof that OKI Company recognized the validity of ADI Company's authorization to Lung Yuen Company and Lung Yuen Company's sub-authorization to Nobel Company.

To perform the four-party agreement, defendant CEIEC Company signed two "Purchase Contracts" with defendant Lung Yuen Company on August 10, 1996, whereby Lung Yuen Company would supply 500 printers and 200 printers respectively, at a unit price of HKD 2,450 each, for a total payment of HKD 1,715,000; delivery was to be before October 15 of the same year, and Lung Yuen Company guaranteed safe shipment from Hong Kong to Wuxi and handover to the purchasing unit, the plaintiff Nobel Company in this case; payment was by letter of credit payable 45 days after delivery. Pursuant to the contracts, CEIEC Company opened letters of credit through Bank of China, Hong Kong Branch, on August 13 and October 1, with Lung Yuen Company as beneficiary, the latest delivery date being October 15, and payment 45 days after delivery, in the amounts of HKD 1,225,000 and HKD 490,000 respectively. Thereafter, Nobel Company actually received a total of 650 printers from October 5 to December 2. CEIEC Company paid HKD 673,750 to Lung Yuen Company on December 9 and HKD 1,041,250 on December 16, totaling HKD 1,715,000.

Because national regulations effective October 1, 1996, required that imported printers must obtain an "Import Commodity Safety and Quality License" issued by the State Commodity Inspection Bureau and affix the approved commodity inspection safety certification mark (CCIB) before they could be allowed into the domestic market, the plaintiff Nobel Company, starting from November 5, 1996, requested defendants Lung Yuen Company and ADI Company: "All received goods do not have the CCIB mark; please resolve this as soon as possible." However, Lung Yuen Company has to date been unable to provide qualified customs clearance and commodity inspection procedures.

It was also found that from October 10, 1996, to January 1997, the plaintiff Nobel Company had sold 129 printers, with 521 printers remaining unsold. From November 1996 to January 1997, Nobel Company paid a total of RMB 679,740 for the printers, including RMB 163,000 to defendant Lung Yuen Company and RMB 516,740 to defendant CEIEC Company. CEIEC Company received funds remitted by Lung Yuen Company and Nobel Company, totaling the equivalent of HKD 585,000.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including: the four-party agreement, the two purchase and sale contracts signed between CEIEC Company and Lung Yuen Company, the letters of credit opened by CEIEC Company and proof of payment at maturity, evidence that Nobel Company actually received 650 printers, payment vouchers from Nobel Company to Lung Yuen Company and CEIEC Company, invoices for Nobel Company's sale of 129 printers, evidentiary materials and payment receipts for Nobel Company's advertising activities, faxes from Nobel Company requesting authorization documents, a fax from ADI Company replying that it was impossible to grant Nobel Company exclusive distributor status, a certificate from OKI Company regarding the authorization, and faxes from Nobel Company requesting Lung Yuen Company to produce customs clearance and commodity inspection certificates.

Opinion of the Court:
The Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held that the "Agreement on the Sale of OKI PAGE-4W Printers in the Chinese Market" signed on August 6, 1996, by the plaintiff Nobel Company and the defendants ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, and CEIEC Company was premised on Nobel Company having the sole exclusive distributorship in the domestic market. As ADI Company had only obtained a non-exclusive sales right from OKI Hong Kong Company for the period from June 1, 1996, to May 31, 1997, and its authorization to Lung Yuen Company and Lung Yuen Company's sub-authorization to Nobel Company had not been recognized by OKI Company, ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company could not guarantee that Nobel Company would be the sole exclusive distributor to perform the four-party agreement. Subsequently, ADI Company, on the grounds that Nobel Company "failed to meet the sales data agreed in the agreement," expressly stated that it was impossible to authorize Nobel Company as the sole agent, causing Nobel Company to face customer questions during advertising and sales, seriously damaging Nobel Company's lawful rights and interests. It should be found that the acts of ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company constituted fraud against Nobel Company by concealing the true facts. Article 10 of the Foreign Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract concluded through fraud or duress is void." The four-party agreement signed is void, and property received by the parties under the agreement shall be returned to the other party. Article 11 provides: "A party that is liable for the invalidity of a contract shall compensate the other party for losses suffered as a result of the invalidity." The losses suffered by Nobel Company due to the invalidity of the contract shall be compensated by ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company. The 521 unsold printers received by Nobel Company under the agreement shall be returned to Lung Yuen Company; for the 129 printers already sold, the equivalent amount of RMB 420,540 shall be returned at the original price; the portion of the paid amount of RMB 679,740 exceeding the return amount, i.e., RMB 259,200, shall be refunded by Lung Yuen Company to Nobel Company. ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company shall compensate Nobel Company for the loss of advertising expenses. Nobel Company, by selling printers without receiving qualified commodity inspection certificates, also bore some fault; therefore, its claims for compensation for transportation and postage costs, travel expenses, and other operating expenses, as well as loss of anticipated profits, are not supported. Nobel Company's request that CEIEC Company refund the purchase price and the price difference is not supported, as CEIEC Company had no fault in making advances for Nobel Company or in the signing and performance of the agreement. Lung Yuen Company shall refund the outstanding advance payment to CEIEC Company. CEIEC Company's request that Lung Yuen Company refund the outstanding amount and losses is not addressed in this case due to insufficient evidence provided.

Judgment:
Accordingly, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. The "Agreement on the Sale of OKI PAGE-4W Printers in the Chinese Market" signed on August 6, 1996, by plaintiff Nobel Company and defendants ADI Company, Lung Yuen Company, and CEIEC Company is void;
2. Plaintiff Nobel Company shall return 521 OKI PAGE-4W printers to defendant Lung Yuen Company;
3. Defendant Lung Yuen Company shall refund RMB 259,200 to plaintiff Nobel Company;
4. Defendant Lung Yuen Company shall refund HKD 113,000 to defendant CEIEC Company;
5. Defendants ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company shall compensate plaintiff Nobel Company for the loss of advertising expenses in the amount of RMB 139,350;
6. All other claims of plaintiff Nobel Company are dismissed.

Litigation costs of RMB 22,000: RMB 2,200 to be borne by plaintiff Nobel Company, and RMB 19,800 to be jointly borne by defendants ADI Company and Lung Yuen Company.

Lung Yuen Company appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Jiangsu High People's Court. The main reasons were: OKI Company's authorization to ADI Company did not preclude ADI Company from having exclusive distribution rights; in fact, ADI Company was the sole distributor in China. Since OKI Company was aware of ADI Company's sub-authorization to Lung Yuen Company as China regional agent and did not object, it should be deemed consent. The first-instance judgment's finding that Lung Yuen Company concealed the truth and committed fraud was unfounded.

Opinion of the Jiangsu High People's Court:
After trial, the Jiangsu High People's Court held that the facts found at first instance were clear and the evidence sufficient. The original defendant ADI Company, knowing that it was not the exclusive distributor of PAGE-4W printers in China and could not grant the sole exclusive distributorship to others, nevertheless authorized Nobel Company as the sole exclusive distributor through Lung Yuen Company. This constituted fraud by concealing the true facts and was the fundamental cause of the invalidity of the four-party agreement. ADI Company bears primary fault for this. The appellant Lung Yuen Company, without obtaining written authorization from ADI Company, sub-authorized Nobel Company, also bearing some fault for causing the invalidity of the contract. However, Lung Yuen Company carried out the sub-authorization after ADI Company expressly authorized it as the China regional agent, and there was no evidence that Lung Yuen Company colluded with ADI Company to defraud Nobel Company. Therefore, the first-instance judgment ordering Lung Yuen Company to bear joint and several liability with ADI Company was improper and should be corrected. Part of Lung Yuen Company's appeal grounds is established and shall be upheld.

Judgment:
Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(ii) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment:

1. Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 of the first-instance civil judgment are affirmed.
2. Item 5 of the first-instance civil judgment and the portion concerning the allocation of case acceptance fees are reversed.
3. The appellee Nobel Company's loss of advertising expenses in the amount of RMB 139,350 shall be compensated by the original defendant ADI Company.

Case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, each RMB 22,000: Nobel Company to bear RMB 2,000 in each instance, ADI Company to bear RMB 12,000 in each instance, and Lung Yuen Company to bear RMB 8,000 in each instance.
